l4_case_applications.application_summary: The inconsistent-positions principle is not confined to inconsistent factual allegations and may apply to inconsistent positions or assumptions adopted in different proceedings.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Lancom Ltd v Capxon International Electronic Co Ltd
l4_case_applications.application_summary: A party adopting a position inconsistent and incompatible with one adopted in previous proceedings may face an abuse-of-process and estoppel objection.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Vasily Trubnikov v Evgeny Volosov and others
l4_case_applications.application_summary: A diametrically opposed later claim advanced with full knowledge of the facts may be abusive because it undermines the integrity of the administration of justice.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Liu Hao Tsing Education Foundation Ltd and another v Liu Tieh Ching Brandon
l4_case_applications.application_summary: Where the relevant facts are plainly within a party's knowledge, inconsistent alternative factual cases may be impermissible.

l4_case_applications.case_name: Shinyei (Shanghai) Trading Co Ltd v Jenus Top Ltd
l4_case_applications.application_summary: A material deviation between a verifying affirmation and the pleaded case may prevent summary judgment because the claim is not verified as pleaded.
